title: One student, five registers: why school data gets typed again and again
excerpt: An admission becomes a register entry, a class list, a fee card, a bus list and a mark sheet — each written by hand, by someone different. Here’s where the time goes, and how to stop it.
author: SmartShala team
body:
When a new student joins, the office doesn’t make one record. It makes five.

The **admission register** gets the student’s details. The **class teacher** copies the name into the attendance register. The **accountant** opens a fee card. If the child takes the bus, someone adds them to the **route list**. And at exam time, the name goes onto every **mark sheet**.

Same child, same spelling — written five times, by five people, in five places.

## Where the time actually goes

Typing is the small part. The real cost shows up later:

- **Mismatches.** A roll number changes in one register but not the others, and a report card goes out with the wrong name.
- **Waiting.** The principal asks how many fees are pending, and someone has to add up the fee cards by hand.
- **Late surprises.** Defaulters are found at the end of term, not when the first instalment is missed.
- **Lost history.** When a register is full, last year’s entries go into a cupboard and are hard to find again.

## One record, many views

The fix isn’t to type faster. It’s to type once.

In SmartShala, a student is added once — with guardian details, Aadhaar and APAAR IDs and documents — and every office reads from that one record. The class teacher sees them on the roll call. The accountant assigns the fee structure for their class. Transport adds them to a route and the fee appears on their ledger. Marks entered by subject teachers flow into one report card.

> Nobody re-types what someone else already entered.

## Getting started without a big bang

You don’t have to move everything at once. Most schools start with:

1. **Student records** — import your existing list in bulk.
2. **Fees** — the module that saves the office the most hours.
3. **Attendance** — because teachers feel the difference on day one.

Everything else can follow when the office is ready.
